audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, initial; Russian loans keep Russian stress) rested on UraTyp database values with no copies we hold and empty quote/cite/loc fields. I downloaded the UraTyp CLDF rows (verbatim match to the record's source text) and the open-access primary grammar UraTyp cites, Grünthal 2015 Vepsän kielioppi, whose p.34 statement 'Paino on ensimmäisellä tavulla. Venäläisperäisissä sanoissa paino noudattaa usein venäjän painotusta.' directly confirms initial primary stress with Russian-origin words often retaining Russian stress -- exactly the fixed-dominant (non-strict) coding. No source seen (UraTyp, Grünthal 2015, Pajusalu et al. 2018, minlang.iling-ran.ru) suggests anything else; UraTyp's UT124=1 concerns secondary stress on the -mine suffix and does not affect primary-stress coding.
